newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turkish, Greek Cypriots reach deal on missing.
newsitem.headline: Turkish, Greek Cypriots reach deal on missing.

text.p: Leaders of Cyprus's Greek and Turkish communities on Thursday reached an agreement that could lead to the opening of mass graves of persons listed as missing in hostilities between the two sides.

The agreeement, a major breakthrough in an issue which has plagued the divided Mediterranean island for decades, was made in the second meeting this week between Cyprus President Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash in Nicosia.

"The two leaders recognise the right of those families whose missing loved ones are proved to be dead to have to the best extent possible their remains for proper burial in line with their religious traditions and practices," U.N. envoy Gustave Feissel told reporters in a statement after the meeting.

"...The two leaders agreed as a first step towards resolving the problem of missing persons to provide each other, immediately and simultaneously, all information already at their disposal on the location of graves of Turkish Cypriot and Greek Cypriot missing persons."
The agreement basically adopts a position Clerides has advocated for years on the simultaneous opening up of graves on either side believed to contain the bodies of missing persons.

The Greek Cypriot side says 1,619 Greek Cypriots are missing since 1974 when Turkish troops invaded and occupied the northern third of Cyprus after a coup in Nicosia engineered by the military then ruling Greece.
Turkish Cypriots say 803 of their community are missing from intercommunal clashes dating back to the 1960s.
Feissel said the two leaders would each designate a representative who by the end of September would exchange information on missing persons and prepare arrangements for the return of remains.
He said the two leaders also agreed that the remains of persons known to have been killed in action on either side be returned to their families.
Clerides and Denktash, standing behind Feissel as he made his announcement, did not make any comments. They smiled, shook hands and left.
Dates for further meetings between the two leaders have not been announced, but Feissel said they indicated their readiness for further meetings.
The talks in Nicosia are held in between U.N.-sponsored talks designed to restart stalled negotiations for an overall settlement to the Cyprus problem.

During Thursday's meeting Denktash was expected to reiterate Turkish Cypriot opposition to Cyprus's accession talks with the European Union, due to start next year, but Feissel said the issue was not discussed.

The Turkish Cypriot side hotly opposes Cyprus's application to become a full EU member, citing international treaties which it says bar the island becoming a member of an institution to which Turkey, one of Cyprus's guarantor powers, does not belong.
The other two guarantor powers are Greece, the closest ally of the Greek Cypriots, and former colonial ruler Britain. Both are EU members.
